tagline: Talk instead of type, in any app on your iPhone.
description: The clean-room iPhone app for murmur, kicked off by US-034 in the desktop prd.json and designed with LaBroi on 2026-10-10, while desktop stands at v0.1.10. A keyboard that is a dictation pad around the waveform pill, backed by the containing app, which holds the microphone, the key, the cleanup, and the history. Bring your own key (Groq by default, any OpenAI-compatible endpoint), the same formatter rules and test vectors as desktop, and a new App Store Connect record under Eze Media LLC. Copyright Eze Media LLC, GPLv3. Nothing from the old iOS app (now Undertone) or the other excluded repos ever enters this repo: concepts only.

stack.language: Swift 6 with strict concurrency. SwiftUI for screens; UIKit only where the keyboard extension needs it (UIInputViewController).
stack.platform: iOS 26 minimum, iPhone first; iPad in IOS-027.
stack.project: XcodeGen recipe at ios/project.yml. The generated .xcodeproj is git-ignored.
stack.core: MurmurCore, a local Swift package at ios/MurmurCore with no UI: formatter, dictionary, expansions, speech gate, WAV encoding, provider catalog, transcription and cleanup clients, history, and the mailbox protocol. Tested with swift test on the Mac, no simulator needed.
stack.targets: The app murmur (com.lbwalton.murmur.ios) and the keyboard extension murmur Keyboard (com.lbwalton.murmur.ios.keyboard), sharing the app group group.com.lbwalton.murmur. Team 4B55ZVBVKN (Eze Media LLC).
stack.sharedData: shared/*.json is copied into the app bundle at build time. Swift never keeps its own copy of a rule.
stack.painting: Screens that paint (the Journey, a painting a day, share cards) run desktop's brush engine, bundled at build time, in a web view with no network access. The keyboard pill is drawn in Swift, because keyboards get little memory.
stack.dependencies: No third-party Swift packages without LaBroi's OK.
stack.toolchain: Xcode 27 with the iOS 26.5 and 27.0 simulators on LaBroi's Mac (checked 2026-10-10).

decisions.scope: The first TestFlight build is core dictation only: the keyboard, the hot mic session, your own key, the formatter with dictionary and expansions, and history. Belts, painting a day, notes, transform, and time back follow as later stories here.
decisions.money: Free download, and the core is free with your own key. murmur Pro is a one-time Apple in-app purchase that never gates the core. Founding members get their ten percent through one-time-use offer codes (offer codes cover one-time purchases; codes expire within 6 months, so they are issued on request). A desktop license key can never unlock anything on iPhone: App Review 3.1.1 bans license keys for unlocking features, and 3.1.3(b) lets purchases carry across platforms only when the same item is also sold in the app (both checked 2026-10-10). Later, Pro adds a done-for-you key sold weekly or monthly, like Wispr Flow, which needs a murmur server (IOS-028).
decisions.keyboard: A dictation pad: the pill, globe, space, delete, and return. Typing letters stays with the other keyboards.
decisions.journey: The iPhone keeps its own Journey for now. One Journey across devices arrives with the murmur account (IOS-029).
decisions.approach: Native Swift reading the same shared/*.json and passing shared/test-vectors.json. Painted screens use desktop's brush engine in a web view so a painting matches the Mac.
decisions.switchback: Nothing public returns you to the app you came from, and since iOS 26.4 not even Wispr Flow does it (checked 2026-10-10). murmur shows you the swipe back instead. Opening murmur from the keyboard uses the responder-chain open that dictation keyboards ship, which needs Full Access; the Control Center and Action Button starts (IOS-016) are the fallback if Apple ever closes it. The auto-return private API stays out of scope (decided 2026-08-09).
decisions.waveforms: The same seven pill styles as desktop, live while you talk: in the keyboard pill, large on the screen you land on after the first tap, on the Look grid, and in first-run practice. Lock Screen and Dynamic Island show a still, clean pill, because iOS redraws them only now and then. Only the pill look ships on iPhone, since the keyboard gives the pill a fixed home. Between takes the pill stays still, even while the session keeps the mic warm.
decisions.contributions: The source is open so anyone can read it and build it. murmur accepts no outside code, so Eze Media LLC stays the sole copyright holder and can ship on the App Store. Issues and ideas are welcome.

conventions.verify: npm run ios:test and npm run ios:smoke must be green before any iOS commit, plus npm run typecheck and npm run test, since ios/ shares shared/ and scripts/ with desktop. Any change to shared/ or to code desktop runs also runs npm run smoke. ios:smoke builds the app for a simulator, runs it headless, and prints SMOKE_RESULT JSON; every subsystem adds a named check.
conventions.stories: Work stories in order. Never set passes true until every acceptance criterion is verified; record how in notes. Stories with needs_human true get built and smoke-verified, then their human step goes into HANDOFF.md and into the chat reply as numbered plain-language steps, and work continues. Live checks run on LaBroi's iPhone from a TestFlight build, signed in to TestFlight as lbwalton@gmail.com (his phone's iCloud is a different Apple Account).
conventions.commits: One commit per story minimum, prefixed with the story id (IOS-005: ...). git pull --rebase before every commit. iOS work lives on feature/ios until LaBroi says to merge. After changing ios/prd.json, run npm run roadmap, which writes both roadmaps.
conventions.review: The review gate applies: before a story's push, an independent reviewer agent examines the full diff against CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, and these conventions. Confirmed findings get fixed and re-verified; disputed ones go to LaBroi.
conventions.cleanRoom: Never open or copy from undertone (including the old iOS app), the-peoples-voice-flow, or OpenWhisp. Concepts yes, artifacts no. Porting murmur's own desktop code to Swift is fine: it is this repo.
conventions.parity: Behavior lives in shared/ and nowhere else. When iOS needs a rule desktop keeps only in TypeScript (the cleanup and transform prompts and their checks, the speech gate's numbers), it moves into shared/ first, desktop reads it from there with unchanged behavior, and both platforms test against the same vectors.
conventions.design: Night studio tokens only: a generator turns src/renderer/tokens.css into a Swift colors file at build time, and the design lint fails raw hex anywhere else in ios/. The pill is the one bold thing; everything around it stays quiet. Every screen uses the system font with Dynamic Type up to the largest accessibility size without clipping; gives every control a VoiceOver label; keeps tap targets at least 44 by 44 points and text contrast at WCAG AA or better; designs its loading, empty, and error states; and gives Reduce Motion still, finished frames. Interface motion settles without bounce; paint motion uses DESIGN.md's four verbs. Copy is plain, sentence case, with active verbs and lowercase murmur; errors say what happened and how to fix it, in clean red. Before building any screen, consult the frontend-design, elite-saas-designer, and ui-skills-root skills (CLAUDE.md). SwiftUI views stay small, own their state with @State and @Observable, load with .task, and ship a preview for each state.
conventions.privacy: Your words and audio go only to the provider you chose, straight from your phone. The core app has no murmur server, no analytics, no tracking, and no ads. The keyboard extension makes no network requests; only the app talks to your provider. The key lives in the Keychain, readable only by the app, on this device only. Audio between takes is never kept or sent. History stays in the app's own container; the keyboard sees only the newest take. Logs never hold your words or any key.
conventions.docs: iPhone docs are written as each story ships, in ios/docs/iphone.md: headings phrased as the questions people ask, short answers first, and a checked-on date for facts that drift. They move into docs/ and onto the website when the App Store page goes live (IOS-026), because the site publishes everything in docs/.
conventions.tooling: No binary assets in the repo: the app icon and screenshots are generated by script, and the display face is fetched at build time as on desktop. npm install, typecheck, test, and smoke never need Xcode; only the ios: scripts do.
conventions.style: No em dashes or spaced hyphens as clause separators anywhere. The product name is always lowercase murmur, on the home screen and in the keyboard list too.

stories.title: MurmurCore passes desktop's answer key
stories.description: The rules that make murmur's text murmur's, in Swift, proven against the same cases desktop runs.
acceptance: MurmurCore runs every vector in shared/test-vectors.json through desktop's pipeline (the dictionary on raw input, formatting from shared/format-spec.json, dictionary casing, then expansions) and every one passes

The speech gate's numbers (window, loudness threshold, minimum voiced time) and the hallucination list (today src/shared/hallucinations.json) move into shared/; desktop reads them from there with unchanged behavior
A new shared vector file of generated tone and silence cases, plus hallucination phrases, passes on both platforms
WAV encoding produces the same bytes as desktop's src/shared/wav.ts on shared sample cases
shared/provider-catalog.json loads into Swift types (presets, models, key prefixes, key pages), and a test fails if a field desktop uses is missing
Desktop's test suite runs the new shared vectors too, so a change in shared/ breaks both platforms or neither
npm run typecheck, npm run test, and npm run smoke stay green after desktop reads from shared/
stories.notes: Verified 2026-10-11 on feature/ios (plan ios/plans/2026-10-10-murmurcore-parity.md, built inline). (1) FormatterVectorTests.matchesDesktop runs all 59 vectors in shared/test-vectors.json through desktop's pipeline (dictionary on raw input, formatting from shared/format-spec.json, dictionary casing, expansions): 59/59 pass, and everyVectorLoaded confirms the decoded count equals the file's count. Sixteen of the 59 are new parity vectors (accents, emoji, a curly apostrophe, ASCII word edges, a $5 dictionary value, a sharp s, the equal-length comma, colon, and new paragraph pairs, and four the final review added for JavaScript's whitespace set and line ends, each shown to fail when that rule is broken in Swift), computed by desktop's own code. The equal-length rule (by symbol, then phrase) is written into format-spec.json and formatter.ts and is today's order, so desktop output is unchanged. (2) shared/speech-gate.json holds the gate's numbers (windowMs 30, rmsThreshold 0.01, minVoicedMs 200, paddingMs 250, deadStreamPeak 0.001) and src/shared/hallucinations.json moved to shared/hallucinations.json (git mv, content unchanged). speech-gate.ts reads its defaults from the shared file; src/shared/speech-gate-shared.test.ts swaps other numbers in and watched all 4 tests fail before the change and pass after. Every existing speech gate test passes unchanged. (3) shared/speech-vectors.json: 11 generated tone and silence signals, 13 whole-transcript hallucination checks, 6 trailing strips. Desktop: src/shared/speech-vectors.test.ts 30/30. Swift: SpeechVectorTests.signalMatchesDesktop 11/11 and hallucinationsMatchDesktop pass. (4) shared/wav-vectors.json: 6 cases (empty, halves where Math.round sends -16383.5 to -16383, clamping, tiny values, ordinary values, a 48 kHz header). Desktop src/shared/wav-vectors.test.ts 6/6; Swift WavVectorTests.bytesMatchDesktop 6/6, plus aNaNSampleWritesZero. (5) ProviderCatalog loads shared/provider-catalog.json (presets, models, key prefixes, key pages). Removing any of the 8 provider fields, 4 catalog fields, or 4 estimate fields desktop's validateCatalog requires fails to load (16 cases), as does a model without an id or an unknown kind. (6) Desktop's suite runs every new shared file: formatter.test.ts (59 vectors), speech-vectors.test.ts, wav-vectors.test.ts. (7) npm run typecheck exit 0, npm run test 845/845, npm run smoke ok after desktop reads from shared/. swift test: 27 tests in 6 suites (SharedData, JS, formatter, speech, WAV, catalog). npm run ios:test: MurmurCore 27/27 and app 9/9. npm run ios:smoke ok with sharedJson true on 12 bundled files. Follow-up 2026-10-11 (LaBroi approved the three deferred review minors): JS.substitute finds the $ by code unit, so a $ fused after a prepended mark (U+0600, U+0D4E) still follows JavaScript's rules; isHallucination and the spoken punctuation symbol order compare code units (JS.same), as JavaScript's === does; everyHallucinationPhraseIsASCII guards normalizeTranscript's lowercasing; the wordsToDigits guard comment is reworded. Each new test failed first (an accented phrase added for one run failed the ASCII guard). The review gate found the parity tests themselves compared strings with Swift's ==, so a canonically equivalent but different output would pass; every string parity check now goes through expectSameUnits (code units), and parityChecksCompareCodeUnits failed against a helper using ==. swift test 31/31.

stories.title: Provider and key setup
stories.description: Bring your own key on the phone: pick a provider, paste a key, and know right away that it works.
acceptance: A Provider screen offers the presets from shared/provider-catalog.json, with Groq first as the default, plus a custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint with base URL and model fields: the same choices desktop offers for transcription and for cleanup
A key ring keeps one saved key per provider, as on desktop, so switching providers never asks for a key twice

Keys are saved in the Keychain, readable only by the app, after first unlock, on this device only (never synced or restored to another device). Key items live in the app's own Keychain access group (its application identifier), never in the shared app group, which also counts as a Keychain access group for both targets; a test saves a key and confirms its access group is the app's own application identifier, never the app group, so the keyboard can never read it
Get a key opens the provider's key page from the catalog. A key with the wrong prefix for its provider gets a gentle inline note, never a block

Test connection makes one small real request and answers inline in plain words: Works, Key rejected (and how to fix it), No connection, or the provider's own message. A saved key only ever shows its last four characters
A key never appears in logs, diagnostics, crash reports, or the pasteboard
Meets conventions.design, with previews for no key, a saved key, testing, works, and each failure
Smoke: a check saves a dummy key, reads it back, and deletes it; another runs Test connection against a local stub for each answer
ios/docs/iphone.md answers How do I add my API key on iPhone? and Where does murmur keep my key?
Live: LaBroi pastes his Groq key and Test connection says Works
stories.notes: Built on feature/ios 2026-10-12 (plan ios/plans/2026-10-11-provider-and-key.md, inline); every automated criterion verified, and the live check waits for TestFlight 1 (IOS-015, HANDOFF). (1) ProviderCatalog.presets(for:) offers Groq, OpenAI, and Mistral for transcription, and Groq, OpenAI, Mistral, DeepSeek, Cerebras, and OpenRouter for cleanup, in catalog order with Groq first and the default (ProviderChoicesTests); Custom takes a base URL and a model for either, and cleanup is Same as transcription or Separate, as on desktop. Rulings: desktop's Local is left out, since localhost on a phone is the phone, and custom addresses must be https, since iOS blocks plain http without an App Transport Security exception; the field says so in red. (2) The key ring files one Keychain item per base URL, normalized as desktop's normalizeUrl does, so switching providers and back shows each saved key again (KeyRingTests.keepsOneKeyPerProvider, ProviderModelTests.switchingProvidersNeverAsksForAKeyTwice). (3) KeychainStore saves after first unlock, this device only (KeychainStoreTests.itemsStayOnThisDeviceAndOpenAfterFirstUnlock). KeyRingTests.keysLiveInTheAppsOwnAccessGroup reads a saved key's access group back: the app's application identifier (team id, a dot, the bundle id), never group.com.lbwalton.murmur; theAccessGroupCheckSeesTheAppGroup shows the check tells the two apart, since an item put in the app group on purpose reads back as the app group. (4) Get a key opens the catalog's keyUrl. KeyNote gives a gentle note for another provider's prefix or a Groq key missing gsk_, and the key still saves (KeyNoteTests, ProviderModelTests.aWrongPrefixGetsANoteAndStillSaves). (5) Test connection sends desktop's probe (GET of the model list with the key, 10 seconds) and answers inline: Works, Key rejected with how to fix it (a 403 also points at the account), No connection, or the provider's own words (ConnectionTestTests, ProviderCopyTests). A saved key shows only four dots and its last four characters (APIKeyTests), and an answer for an address the person already left is dropped (ProviderModelTests.aLateAnswerNeverLandsOnAnotherProvider, seen failing first). (6) APIKey prints, interpolates, and dumps only its mask (APIKeyTests.printingAKeyNeverShowsIt); a provider message that repeats the key shows the mask instead (ConnectionTestTests.aMessageNeverRepeatsTheKey); the key field is a SecureField, so the key cannot be copied out; the choices live in the app's own defaults and never hold a key (ProviderModelTests.aKeyNeverReachesTheDefaults, and the smoke checks the app's defaults); the app writes no logs. (7) Night studio tokens only (design lint clean); sentence case; a VoiceOver label on every control and an announcement for each answer; system rows for tap targets; previews for no key, the wrong prefix, a saved key, testing, works, key rejected, no connection, and a provider message, plus the whole screen with and without a key, reviewed in simulator captures before the plan. Remove key asks first, and only the confirming button is red. (8) npm run ios:smoke: keyRing (a dummy key saved, read back, found in the app's own access group, absent from the defaults, deleted) and connectionTest (an in-app URLProtocol stand-in gives each of the four answers through URLSession) are both true, beside appGroup, keychain, and sharedJson. (9) ios/docs/iphone.md answers How do I add my API key on iPhone? and Where does murmur keep my key? Review gate (an independent opus reviewer over 57a3485..7e2bcb5): no Critical; four findings fixed, each with a test seen failing first: the key is now masked before a long provider message is cut (ConnectionTestTests.aKeyAcrossTheCutIsStillMasked), editing a custom address keeps a pasted key (ProviderModelTests.editingACustomAddressKeepsThePastedKey), an address of a preset the role leaves out stays Custom (anAddressThisRoleDoesNotOfferStaysCustom), and a custom provider with no address reads Paste your key (ProviderCopyTests.anUnnamedProviderReadsNaturally). At the largest text size the screen reflows without clipping (simulator capture). After the push, CI (Xcode 26.6, Swift 6.3.3) crashed the compiler on ProviderScreen: it cannot turn a stored main-actor closure into Binding's setter, which Swift 6.4 here compiles. The screen now binds every field by key path to settable properties on ProviderModel, pinned by ProviderModelTests.theFieldsChangeTheSavedChoices and theProviderPickerChoosesById. stories.title: Record and transcribe in the app
stories.description: The first real take: speak in the app, get your words back, and never get words for silence.
acceptance: The app records mono audio through AVAudioSession and asks for the microphone, with a plain purpose string, the first time it needs it

Smoke: a check runs a generated tone and a generated silence through the gate; another sends a take to a local stub server and reads the words back

stories.title: The dictation pad
stories.description: The keyboard: one big pill to talk, and just enough keys to finish the job.
acceptance: The keyboard shows the pill in the middle with globe, space, delete, and return around it. Globe moves to the next keyboard and a long press lists them; delete repeats while held; return follows the field's return key type

Tapping the pill starts a take, and tapping again stops it. The keyboard tells the app through Darwin notifications (start, stop, cancel); the app answers through a mailbox file in the app group plus a words ready signal

If you left the field before the words landed, Insert last appears in the keyboard and inserts the newest take when tapped; the take is also in history in the app
In password and phone number fields, iOS shows Apple's keyboard instead, and murmur leaves it that way
Without Full Access, the keyboard shows one short line on why it needs it, with the exact steps to turn it on
The keyboard makes no network requests; a test fails if keyboard code uses URLSession or any other networking API
The keyboard stays inside the extension memory limit through a long session, checked with Instruments on LaBroi's iPhone and recorded in notes
Meets conventions.design: every key has a VoiceOver label, targets are at least 44 points, and labels never clip at any text size the keyboard height allows
Smoke: a mailbox round trip, in which the app posts a take, a simulated keyboard reads it once, and a second read gets nothing

stories.title: The hot mic session and the swipe back
stories.description: How a take works from any app: the first tap opens murmur already listening, you swipe back, and the mic stays ready until you are done.
acceptance: When no session is running, tapping the pill opens murmur through the responder-chain open (Full Access required), and murmur starts a session and a take at once

That screen shows the live waveform large, the word Recording, and an animated guide along the bottom edge showing the swipe right that returns to your app. Words spoken before you swipe back count. Reduce Motion shows the guide as a still arrow and one sentence

The session ends after the length you pick, counted from your last take: 5 minutes, 15 minutes (the default), or 1 hour. End session ends it at once, in the app and in the keyboard, where a long press on the pill opens a small menu that holds it (IOS-023 and IOS-024 add Note and Transform to the same menu)
A phone call, Siri, or another app taking the mic ends the session cleanly; a take in progress stops and is processed as if you tapped stop
Music or a podcast that is playing when a session starts keeps playing
If iOS ever refuses to open murmur from the keyboard, the pill says Open murmur to start, and the docs point to the other ways in (IOS-016)

Each take adds lines built only from ActivityEvent (numbers, flags, fixed names, an 8 character take id): captured with its length, peak, and voiced time; heard nothing with the same numbers and whether it was sent; failed with its kind (unknown kinds become other) and only the http status or URL error number from its detail, and whether the audio was saved; cancelled before it was sent, with its length; words as a count; mic off; mic failed; retried takes marked. Settings, Diagnostics says what a report holds and never holds; Save report builds one text file (murmur version and build, iOS version, device model, whether the keyboard has reported with Full Access, session length and whether one runs, transcription and cleanup as preset names or custom, model ids murmur lists or only the length of one typed by hand, whether a key is saved, formatting, dictionary and expansion counts, waiting and history counts, the pill style, and the last 200 log lines), saves it to the app's temporary folder replacing the last, and opens it as a preview; Share there opens the share sheet (the text itself if the file could not be written). The keyboard: with text selected, the pill's long-press menu offers Transform (a menu item built each time the menu opens, so a field that keeps its selection from keyboards never shows it); iOS gives keyboards only the first and last sentences of a longer selection (Apple bug FB7789012, still reported in March 2026), so the keyboard trusts the selection whole only when it is one sentence of at most 300 characters, by its own splitter (closing quotes, CJK and Devanagari stops, and line breaks count) and by Foundation's sentence finder alike, and takes a longer one from the clipboard only when it was copied after the keyboard saw that selection (the clipboard's change count, never asking to paste) and holds every piece of the selection the keyboard saw, in order, or says For more than a sentence, tap Copy first, then Transform. The ask carries the whole selection to murmur; the take model hears the instruction with the dictionary only and keeps it out of history; the bridge refuses a selection it cannot send before anything is heard (no key, over 8,000 characters) and otherwise sends the instruction and the selection through the cleanup connection, holding background time; the mailbox gives the keyboard the rewrite with the original beside it, or the line saying why the selection stays. The rewrite goes in only while the keyboard still sees the same selection in the same field, looking once more 0.6 seconds later before Insert last holds it, and once it is in, the original takes its place for Insert last; an offered rewrite has no original, Delete everything in murmur clears a waiting original too, and an ask murmur never answered is withdrawn when its take ends. Rulings (LaBroi can overturn any): the product id is the bundle id with .pro; a founding member is a purchase with an offer code named founders (any case); the smoke uses a stand-in made from the same configuration; Pro listens to the App Store from launch; profiles hold the whole setup, and without Pro they wait untouched; early access has nothing to hold yet on iPhone; the murmur Pro row sits after Notes; App Store Connect work (the purchase, its price, the founders offer, sandbox codes) is LaBroi's. Review gate (opus, 2026-10-15): ready with fixes; every fix came with a test seen failing first. Important: leaving murmur Pro before the App Store answered could blank the price or read a buyer as free, and an older read landing late could overwrite a newer one (a cancelled ask now changes nothing, and an answer older than one already kept is dropped); the real purchase path went untested (the StoreKit story now buys through Get murmur Pro's own path and sees the refund through the App Store's updates alone); HANDOFF lacked the Paid Applications Agreement and a fallback for redeeming a sandbox code. Re-graded and fixed: cancelling Restore showed a red connection error (now silent); an unverified purchase said Nothing was charged (now its own line pointing to Restore purchases); the screen said not for sale while the App Store had not answered, and kept old messages (now it waits with Asking the App Store and starts clean); previews for every state; the Name this setup alert moved to the form, with Save waiting for a name; ProCopy's mark line renamed. Deferred minors: the updates loop outlives a non-shared store (tests and smoke only); saved profiles that ever fail to decode read as none and the next save overwrites them. CI: StoreKit's test environment is broken on iOS 26.3 to 26.x simulators (Apple FB22237318, Apple's forums, checked 2026-10-15; reproduced here on iOS 26.5, where no configuration loads), and CI's runner has iOS 26.5, so ProStoreKitTests skips itself there with that reason and runs on iOS 27 here; the stand-in tests and the smoke's pro check run everywhere.
